sections.title: Medical SEO for clinics and healthcare providers
sections.text: A patient may start by asking about a symptom, then search for a specialty or service, and then compare doctors, appointment times and locations. We organize your medical website so they find clear information about the service, the doctor, the branch and the next step to book. In this sector, content must be accurate and reviewed by your medical team; we don't use treatment claims or unverified testimonials to boost visibility.

sections.text: A visitor may start by searching for a symptom that worries them, then try to find the right specialty, and then look at a specific service or doctor and a branch near them. We organize your site's pages so they can move between these steps without general information getting mixed up with the booking page.

items.heading: Branch page

sections.heading: Accurate content with a traceable source
sections.text: Publishing an article that repeats the name of a condition or procedure isn't enough. Medical content is reviewed by a specialist chosen by the provider, and the qualifications of whoever delivers the service and the limits of the published information are made clear. We work on headings, on linking articles to services and doctors, and on mobile readability, while keeping educational information separate from advice that requires an individual assessment by a doctor. We never attribute a specialty or treatment outcome to a clinic that the clinic hasn't approved.

sections.label: How do we measure?
sections.title: From clicks to appointment requests
sections.text: We review the performance of specialty, service and doctor pages in Search Console, then track whether visitors go on to call or request an appointment, where those actions can be measured.

items.text: We have a documented case of a medical services website whose clicks rose from 825 to 12.9K across two consecutive 28-day periods.
This is a visibility and clicks result; we don't describe it as bookings or revenue.

sections.label: Documented result
sections.title: From 825 to 12.9K clicks in 28 days
sections.text: For a medical services website, organic clicks rose from 825 in the previous period to 12.9K in the last 28 days.

items.question: Who reviews the medical articles?
items.answer: A specialist chosen by your organization. We write and structure the content for search, and no medical text is published until your medical team has reviewed it.

items.question: Does every doctor need their own page?
items.answer: Only when patients search for the doctor by name or the doctor is a factor in their decision. Otherwise, the specialty and service pages matter more, with the doctors mentioned on them.

items.question: How do we link each service to the right branch?
items.answer: On the service page, we list the branches that actually offer it, and we link each branch to its own page showing the address and how to book.

items.question: Do more clicks mean more bookings?
items.answer: Not necessarily. We only measure bookings and calls when they're set up to be tracked, and we never describe clicks as bookings.
